title: Paridyum Test-Type Registry
description: The complete id-space of Paridyum test types, declared under ADR-0029. Every TST- id named in any artifact's `verified_by`, and every test type a standard or a CI workflow refers to by name, MUST appear here. This is the fifth registry in the pattern ADR-0014 started: a list that must be extended, moved out of the places where extending it is expensive. `axes` and `tiers` are declared in the same file rather than as enums in this schema because a new axis or tier is registry data too — putting them here would reintroduce the defect. Validated by `knowledge.test_registry_valid`. Only the JSON Schema subset implemented by scripts/lib/validate-schema.py is used: no $ref, no $defs, no propertyNames, no oneOf.

version.description: Manifest format version. Bump only for a breaking shape change, which needs an ADR.

axes.description: The dimensions of failure a test type can address. An axis is NOT an umbrella test type: 'security testing' and 'reliability testing' are axes, not things a repository can own a suite of, and declaring them as test types is how a taxonomy acquires entries nothing can ever satisfy or evidence.

tiers.description: When a test type runs. A tier is the answer to 'what does this cost, and who is waiting for it' — the single decision that keeps a large matrix runnable. A suite with no tier runs everywhere or nowhere, and both are failures.

trigger.description: The event that starts this tier. An event, not a cadence — 'nightly' is a schedule, 'every push to a pull request' is a trigger.

budget.description: The wall-clock this tier may consume before it is the bottleneck. A tier with no budget grows until people route around it.

blocking.description: Whether a failure in this tier stops the change. False is a legitimate answer and must be stated, because a non-blocking tier nobody reads is indistinguishable from an absent one.

test_types.description: One entry per test type. Sorted by id, ascending, so diffs stay readable. Uniqueness of `test_type` and of `name` is enforced by the gate, not expressible here.

test_type.description: Immutable. Never reused, never renumbered — the same rule artifact ids follow, for the same reason: this id is the permanent handle in an artifact's `verified_by`, in a CI job name, and in a test module path.

name.description: The kebab-case handle used in CI job names and test module paths. Unique across the registry.

axis.description: Must be a declared axis. Checked by the gate against `axes`, not by an enum here.

tier.description: Must be a declared tier. Checked by the gate against `tiers`.

status.description: `required` — a repository matching `applies_to` that has none of this is in violation. `recommended` — expected where the shape applies, never gated, because no check can tell whether it applies. `deferred` — real, not startable, and MUST carry a `trigger`. Same three-way distinction ADR-0018 makes for requirements, and for the same reason: a taxonomy that marks everything required is one nobody can comply with, and one that marks nothing required is a glossary.

trigger.description: REQUIRED when status is `deferred`. The event that makes this test type startable — an event, not a date. A deferred test type without one is a TODO with an id.

detects.description: The failure class this test type catches that no cheaper type catches. Phrased as a defect, not as an activity. If it cannot be written without naming a tool, the entry is a tool preference rather than a test type.

evidence.description: The machine-readable artifact a run produces — junit.xml, an lcov file, a SARIF report, a k6 summary. This is what turns 'we test that' into something answerable after the fact, and it is the field that makes SSDF PO.3.3 true rather than claimed. `none` is a legal value and an admission.

artifacts.description: Machine-readable counterpart to `evidence`. STD-0014. `evidence` is prose written for a person and is never parsed — reading it would make its English load-bearing, which ANTI-0008 forbids. This field is the interface. Optional: a type producing nothing collectable (a manual review, a drill) omits it, and that omission is a fact a report can state rather than a gap it must guess at.

kind.description: What the file is, from a closed list. A new kind is a deliberate addition here, not a free-text guess at the producer.

path.description: Path relative to the repository root, as the producing job writes it. OPTIONAL, because it is stack-dependent: TST-0001 lands at reports/junit-unit.xml under TypeScript and target/nextest/ci/junit.xml under Rust. A type used by one stack can name an exact path; one spanning stacks either omits it — declaring only that the artifact kind exists — or gives an entry per stack.

stack.description: Which stack this entry describes, where the path differs between them. Absent means the entry applies to every stack the type declares.

optional.description: True where the artifact is produced only on some runs — a trace kept on failure, for instance. Absent means always produced, so a missing file is a defect.

stacks.description: Which stacks this test type binds, from class-registry.yaml's stack vocabulary, plus `any` for stack-independent types. Absent means `any`.

applies_to.description: Glob over repository names, the same shape as an artifact's `applies_to`. Absent means every repository in the stacks named above.

checks.description: Check ids from check-registry.yaml that enforce the existence or the shape of this suite. An empty list is honest and common: most test types are governed by a standard's prose and evidenced by their artifact, not by a check that can see them.

governed_by.description: Artifact ids that state the rules for this test type. This is the reverse of an artifact's `verified_by` and the gate checks nothing about the reverse direction on purpose — a standard may govern a type it does not itself claim to be verified by.

frameworks.description: Outward mappings to external framework identifiers, keyed by framework, exactly as check-registry.yaml does it and validated the same way (knowledge.framework_ids_resolve against framework-registry.yaml). ADR-0028's direction rule holds here too: a test type exists because something here needs it, never because a framework named it.

declared.description: When this id entered the registry. Never changes, including when the type moves from deferred to required.

notes.description: Boundary cases, the neighbouring type it is confused with, and known false-positive shapes. Not the rationale; that lives in the governing artifact.
